page: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, indicating that hyperthreading is disabled. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is provided by a local 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 3074.87. However, multi-core performance is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, measuring 66.32 GB/sec for read operations and 41.46 GB/sec for write operations, while cached small-block read bandwidth is weak at 294.13 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits weak performance in database operations, with Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations scoring in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is poor, registering at 2.54 GB/sec. For language model tasks, the server achieves an average text generation speed of 138.1 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but drops to a poor 10.87 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. These metrics suggest the server is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel processing or intensive database write operations, such as lightweight caching, text processing, or single-threaded applications.
description: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized virtual server utilizing the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 2 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 50 GB local NVMe SSD. While single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, multi-core and parallel processing benchmarks are weaker, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores falling in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, but cached small-block reads are weak. The server exhibits poor static web serving throughput and weak database operations, making it less suitable for high-concurrency web hosting or heavy database writes. Instead, its high memory-to-core ratio and strong single-core performance make it appropriate for memory-bound, single-threaded tasks, lightweight caching, and basic text processing workloads.
